The retail decision · Data to decisions

Work with the same data.

Every lesson is generated from one store history, with one seed and stable identifiers.

Teach directly from the website

Open a lesson and choose Present lesson. Use the arrow keys or Previous and Next, the slide menu to jump to a topic, and Home or End to reach the first or last slide. Escape exits presentation mode. Slides show concise points and worked visuals. Notes adds the full paragraph explanation beside them; it is visible on the same screen, not a private presenter display.

Full screen expands the presentation when the browser permits it. Print slides opens the browser print dialog for a landscape slide handout or PDF. Read this section returns to the current topic in the continuous lesson. Reading and presentation are two views of the same authored content.

Download the shared records

  • stores.csv — One store per row; cohort, delivery time, location, and baseline profile
  • raw-baseline.csv — The initial export for weeks 1–8, including the defects repaired in Lesson 1
  • baseline-repairs.csv — The ledger records used to reconcile flagged keys
  • baseline.csv — Clean weeks 1–16 for baseline and forecasting work
  • shelf-audit.csv — The independent week-16 audit of 30 sampled stores
  • store-weeks.csv — All 32 weeks, including actual offers, active policy, and outcomes

The complete store-week file is a retrospective record. Use the release and input timing specified in each lesson; the baseline download excludes the future offer and active-policy labels.

Read the fields before fitting a model

Shared data dictionary
FieldMeaning and timing
store_id, weekTogether identify one observation; the store is the assignment unit
cohortPilot, Voluntary, or Rollout; fixed and disjoint
lead_days, urbanKnown store attributes before each study
exposure140 scheduled product-days per week
stockout_days, stockout_rateCount and percentage observed during the target week
demand_forecast, promotion_planPrepared before the target week starts
demand_indexRealized during the week; unavailable to its advance forecast
lag_ratePrevious week’s observed stockout rate
offerRetrospective study assignment/adoption label; excluded from baseline forecasting
activeWhether the offer is operating in this week
operating_cost6 CU per stockout product-day plus 20 CU when active

Run the lesson calculations

Each standalone Python lab includes the shared generator and its lesson’s worked calculation. Each notebook contains the same source in a shared setup cell, followed by the worked steps and saved output. Run all cells from the beginning; no data download or network call is needed by the lab.

Inspect the model and release contract

Shared generator and analysis source · Case specification and data fingerprint · All lesson results

The fingerprint identifies the same public store-week record across all ten result files. The source also retains the alternate policy outcomes used for known-answer comparisons.

Run a downloaded lab

Use Python 3.11 or later. Download the dependency list below and a standalone lesson lab into the same folder. Install the listed packages, then run the lab. It prints the lesson’s results after executing and checking the worked calculation.

Download requirements.txt

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python lesson1-lab.py

To rebuild the complete website, use the instructions in the course source repository.

Reading and accessibility

All lessons, worked answers, and tables are available without an account. Charts include descriptive text and their values in tables. The course works without JavaScript; keyboard users can follow the roadmap and open the answer disclosures.
